title: assert-main-fast-forward.test.sh's report+gate is position-based, not trap-based
description: Filing only, per opum-agent's dispatch (2026-09-28) — do not fix yet. scripts/test/assert-main-fast-forward.test.sh gates its exit code on `[ $fail -eq 0 ]` being the physical last statement in the file (confirmed: lines 361-364 are literally the file's last lines, verdict_reached=yes / blank echo / the report line / the gate, with nothing appended below on origin/dev as of this filing, sha to be recorded from the branch this task is created against). The file already has an EXIT trap (line 117, trap cleanup EXIT) with a cleanup() that handles an ABORT BEFORE the verdict (verdict_reached != yes -> prints PROOF ABORTED EARLY and re-exits with the aborting rc). That trap does nothing once verdict_reached is yes, so a check appended AFTER the report+gate would run, and the trap's cleanup() would no-op and let bash's normal exit-code-of-last-command behavior take over -- the appended command's own exit status, not $fail, would become the script's exit code, and the printed "passed/failed" summary would go stale by construction. Not live today: nothing sits below the gate, so nothing currently exploits this. opum-doc hit and fixed the identical defect in its own copy of this file as ODOC-228 (opum-ai/opum-doc#518, promoted to opum-doc main at b4f405735307dbe5cd56555028f9b97cff1c31df -- both the PR body and the promoted commit read directly, not taken on relay). Its fix moves the report and the exit-code gate into cleanup() itself, unconditional, computed from the live $fail and the rc that triggered the trap: exit 1 if $fail != 0 OR rc != 0, else 0 -- a trap fires exactly once at whatever point the script actually ends, so early-abort and late-addition become the same code path, and position in the file stops deciding what "last" means. It gates on $fail OR rc together deliberately: rc alone would regress to the original defect (an appended command that returns 0 despite calling the harness's own no() would still report green); $fail alone would let an appended crash that never reaches no() get silently swallowed into green. opum-doc proved it two ways: a deliberate post-report failure appended to a scratch copy goes red (both in the fail count and the exit code) on the fixed version while going green with a stale count on the unfixed version, and a clean tree stays green with an unchanged pass/fail count. opum-doc's PR also documents this file as a second deliberate divergence from opum-marketplace's own reference copy (the first being its ODOC-211), at the file's own provenance header -- so porting this fix here is expected to touch that header too, not just the trap logic.

acceptanceCriteria.text: scripts/test/assert-main-fast-forward.test.sh moves the report ("passed $pass, failed $fail") and the exit-code gate into cleanup() itself, computed from the live $fail and the trap rc, so both an early abort and anything appended after the verdict resolve through the same code path
The fix exits non-zero if $fail != 0 OR the trapped rc != 0, and exits 0 only when both are clean, matching the reasoning behind opum-doc ODOC-228 for checking both rather than either alone

Proven the same way ODOC-228 proved its own fix: a deliberate post-verdict failure appended to a disposable scratch copy of the script goes red (non-zero exit, and the failure is named in the fail count) on the fixed version, and a clean tree (the actual tracked file) stays green with an unchanged pass/fail count and exit 0

This change does not simply mirror the opum-doc fix as a blind port; where the opum-marketplace and opum-doc copies of this file are already documented as deliberately divergent (the opum-doc ODOC-211 and ODOC-228 provenance header), the change to the opum-marketplace copy made by this task is evaluated and recorded on its own terms

finalSummary: Fixed the position-based verdict in scripts/test/assert-main-fast-forward.test.sh: the report and the exit-code gate were the physical last lines of the file, so anything appended below them ran uncounted - an appended no() call (which only echoes and returns 0) printed FAIL while the script exited 0, with the printed summary stale by construction, because the EXIT trap's cleanup() no-opped once the verdict was reached. cleanup() now prints the report and computes the gate from live state: exit 1 if $fail != 0 OR the trapped rc != 0, else 0 - a trap fires exactly once at whatever point the script actually ends, so early abort and late addition take one code path. Gating on both is deliberate: $fail alone would let appended code that crashes on its own (never reaching no()) exit green; rc alone is what the unfixed script effectively did. Mirrors opum-doc ODOC-228 (opum-ai/opum-doc#518, promoted b4f4057) but evaluated on this copy's own terms rather than blindly ported - this file's workflow-wiring tail differs from theirs (for-pair vs for-mapping) so only the report+gate moved, and the ODOC-216 environment line stays at the top where this copy shipped it, recorded at the provenance header. Proven on scratch copies with the suite's own harness: unfixed + injected post-verdict no() exits 0 with a stale 'passed 19, failed 0' (defect reproduced); fixed + the same injection exits 1 with 'passed 19, failed 1'; fixed + an appended crash that never calls no() exits 1 via rc alone; the clean tracked file stays 'passed 19, failed 0', exit 0. bash -n clean. Delivered in opum-ai/opum-marketplace#176; CI run 36470496287 green on d3cfc03dbb565e01fa999f8cc28f9867c9a4d2ac (check · manifests, Tracker integrity, lore check all pass).
